doc.title: Administrative Web App
doc.paragraph: This is the web application, developed using Javascript and Adaptive Layouts to create this interactive app. The Administrative Web Application is not required for functionality, but it may be helpful for quickly developing your Adaptive Application.

The app is served by a web server such as Nginx (see the sample configuration in the Appendix) at /apps/afw/admin/, and talks to afwfcgi through the same server: it reads objects with REST requests and calls functions with POST /afw actions. Everything it does is therefore subject to the application's authorization, and anything it shows can also be reached with afw or REST.

section.title: Home
section.paragraph: The starting page, with a short description of, and a link to, each of the sections below.

section.title: Objects
section.paragraph: Browse, query and edit the objects of any adapter: choose an adapter and object type, filter the list with a query, and open an object to view or change it. Objects can also be created, uploaded and edited in batches.

list.item: Status, Server and Application show the state of the server and the application configuration.

Services lists every service and lets you add, edit, start, stop and restart those defined in the configuration adapter. Adapters, Logs and Authorization Handlers show each kind of service. The editor of an LMDB adapter has an Indexes tab (see the chapter).
Request Handlers and Extensions show what is configured and loaded.
Schema edits the object types of an adapter, and Models edits Adaptive Models.

Provisioning and Authorization are placeholders for future pages; configure authorization as described in the
chapter.

section.title: Documentation
section.paragraph: A reference built from the running instance: functions, data types, layout components and the object types of each adapter, with schema diagrams. Because it is generated live, it includes what extensions and models add.

list.item: Fiddle evaluates Adaptive Scripts, expressions and templates on the server, which is a quick way to run administrative functions such as index_create.
Requests composes and sends requests to the server and shows the responses.
